props.title: Old School
props.initialSlug: Three men relive college glory by starting a frat

sections.content: Old School (2003) perfectly captures early 2000s comedy's sweet spot between raunchy humor and heart. Following Will Ferrell's breakout in Anchorman (2004), this film helped establish the Frat Pack era of comedy alongside Wedding Crashers (2005) and The 40-Year-Old Virgin (2005). Director Todd Phillips crafted a spiritual successor to Animal House (1978), updating the fraternity mayhem formula for Gen-X adults trying to recapture their youth. The film's genius lies in casting against type - Luke Wilson as the straight man, Vince Vaughn as a settled family guy, and Will Ferrell unleashing pure chaos as Frank "The Tank."

sections.content: The film sparked a wave of "manchild comedies" exploring arrested development and midlife crises through outrageous scenarios. Step Brothers (2008) took the concept to absurd extremes, while The Hangover (2009) - also directed by Phillips - refined the formula of middle-aged men behaving badly. These films tapped into millennial anxiety about adulthood and responsibility, using crude humor to mask deeper questions about masculinity and maturity in modern America.

The casting proved crucial to Old School's success and lasting influence. Luke Wilson brought genuine pathos to Mitch, making his quarter-life crisis relatable rather than pathetic. Vince Vaughn perfected his rapid-fire delivery style that would define films like Dodgeball (2004) and Wedding Crashers (2005). Will Ferrell's unhinged performance as Frank the Tank became instantly iconic, cementing his transition from SNL to movie stardom. Their chemistry elevated what could have been a simple gross-out comedy into something more memorable. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Influence

sections.content: Old School's DNA can be seen throughout modern comedy, from the improvised riffing style to the blend of raunch and romance. Films like 21 Jump Street (2012) and Neighbors (2014) followed its template of mining humor from the generation gap. The movie also helped establish Todd Phillips as a major director, leading to his eventual dramatic turn with Joker (2019). While some of its humor hasn't aged perfectly, Old School remains influential for showing how R-rated comedy could balance outrageous gags with genuine character development.
